// AUTO-GENERATED by puerto. Edit puerto.toml, then run `puerto generate bootstrap`; add a
// consumer with `puerto generate consumer <name> --on <event_type>`.
use infrastructure::db::events::PgOutbox;
use puerto_events::{Loops, WorkerConfig};
use puerto_kafka::{KafkaConfig, KafkaPublisher};

/// The relay and one consumer per `[[consumer]]`, on the `kafka` transport: the relay publishes
/// each event to its aggregate's topic, `<KAFKA_TOPIC_PREFIX>.<aggregate>`, and each consumer is a
/// consumer group on the topics of its events. Dead letters stay in Postgres.
pub async fn build_worker(config: WorkerConfig) -> Result<Loops, String> {
    let database_url = std::env::var("DATABASE_URL").map_err(|_| {
        "DATABASE_URL is not set — set it in .env (.env.example has one)".to_string()
    })?;
    let pool = infrastructure::db::create_postgres_pool(&database_url)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| format!("{e} — is the database up? `make docker-compose/up`"))?;
    infrastructure::db::run_migrations(&pool, &infrastructure::db::MIGRATOR)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let kafka = KafkaConfig::from_env("shop").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    kafka.ensure_topics(&["product"]).await.map_err(|e| {
        format!("cannot create the Kafka topics: {e} — is the broker up? `make docker-compose/up`")
    })?;
    let publisher = KafkaPublisher::new(&kafka)
        .map_err(|e| format!("cannot create the Kafka producer: {e}"))?;

    Ok(Loops::new(&config).relay(PgOutbox::new(pool), publisher))
}
